cards.explanation: The answer is the crossroads and the city gates. Wisdom takes her stand "…at the crossroads…" (Proverbs 8:2). She also cries out at "…the gates to the city…" (Proverbs 8:3). Crossroads and city gates, out in the open, friends. That's a woman who wants to be heard.

The answer is that she wants them to learn to be shrewd and gain understanding. She says, "O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding." (Proverbs 8:5) She isn't calling them names and walking off, friends. She's calling them to learn. I've been called worse in a junk drawer, and nobody offered me understanding.
The answer is False. Wisdom says, "All the words of my mouth are righteous; none are crooked or perverse." (Proverbs 8:8) She doesn't leave room for a few crooked ones. It's every word, friends.

The answer is False. Wisdom says her words are "…all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge." (Proverbs 8:9) They're plain, not puzzling, friends. I wish my recipe cards were that clear.

The answer is that she is more precious than rubies. Wisdom says, "For wisdom is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire compares with her." (Proverbs 8:11) That's her reason for choosing instruction over silver and gold, friends. Nothing you want makes the comparison.

The answer is to hate evil. Wisdom says, "To fear the LORD is to hate evil…" (Proverbs 8:13) She goes on to name some of what she hates, like evil conduct and perverse speech. So fearing the LORD isn't only a feeling, friends. It comes with hating evil.

The answer is True. She says, "I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech." (Proverbs 8:13) I once stood admiring my own cookies through the oven window for ten whole minutes. I'm working on it, friends.
The answer is kings. Wisdom says, "By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws…" (Proverbs 8:15) Even the people with crowns are on her list, friends. Just laws come through her.

The answer is True. Wisdom says, "I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me." (Proverbs 8:17) Notice that it's a promise for those who seek her early, friends. Those are the ones who will find her.

The answer is that she makes them full. Wisdom is "…bestowing wealth on those who love me and making their treasuries full." (Proverbs 8:21) She doesn't just hand over a little wealth, friends. She fills the treasuries.

The answer is earth. Wisdom says, "From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began." (Proverbs 8:23) She's talking about a time before the ground under our feet existed, friends. That's a long way back.
The answer is True. Wisdom says, "I was there when He established the heavens…" (Proverbs 8:27) She's talking about the skies being set in place, friends. That's a big moment to be present for.

The answer is that He sets a boundary for the sea. Wisdom says He "…set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command…" (Proverbs 8:29) The sea has a line it doesn't cross, friends. And the line comes from His command.

The answer is His delight. Wisdom says, "Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day, rejoicing always in His presence." (Proverbs 8:30) Day by day, friends, not once in a while. And she was rejoicing the whole time.

The answer is False. Wisdom says she was "…rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men." (Proverbs 8:31) She says she delights in them, friends. That's the opposite of keeping her distance.

The answer is ignore it. Wisdom says, "Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it." (Proverbs 8:33) I spent years in a junk drawer full of instruction manuals nobody ever read. Trust me, friends, they're better in your hands.

The answer is favor. Wisdom says, "For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD." (Proverbs 8:35) Two things come with finding her, friends: life and the LORD's favor. That's a good deal.

The answer is that he harms himself. Wisdom says, "…he who fails to find me harms himself…" (Proverbs 8:36) Notice who gets hurt, friends. It's the one who didn't find her. After that she says, "all who hate me love death." (Proverbs 8:36)
